title: Francis Hydro Turbine
subtitle: Water enters a spiral, turns a runner and leaves through a draft tube
scale: ≈ 3.7 m tall · 1.2 m runner · 150 MW class
summary: A Francis turbine is the workhorse of hydroelectric power. Water enters through a spiral casing that distributes it evenly around the runner, guide vanes direct it onto curved blades, and the runner turns the shaft. The draft tube recovers the remaining velocity before the water leaves, which is where much of the efficiency comes from.

parts.name: Foundation
parts.short: The concrete block that carries the machine
parts.detail: The foundation anchors the casing and generator and resists the torque and vibration of the runner.

parts.name: Spiral Casing
parts.short: Distributes water evenly around the runner
parts.detail: The cross-section shrinks as the casing wraps around, so every guide vane receives the same flow.

parts.name: Stay Ring
parts.short: The structural ring inside the casing
parts.detail: The stay ring ties the casing to the foundation and carries the guide-vane mechanism.

parts.name: Stay Vanes
parts.short: Remove swirl before the guide vanes
parts.detail: Fixed vanes straighten the flow and support the stay ring. They do not move during operation.

parts.name: Guide Vanes
parts.short: Control how much water reaches the runner
parts.detail: The guide vanes pivot together. Opening them admits more water and increases power; closing them shuts the machine down.

parts.name: Guide-Vane Ring
parts.short: Links all the vanes to the governor
parts.detail: A regulating ring and links move every guide vane by the same angle, keeping the flow symmetrical.

parts.name: Runner Hub
parts.short: The centre the blades are fixed to
parts.detail: The hub carries the blades and transfers their torque to the shaft.

parts.name: Runner Blades
parts.short: Curved blades that extract the energy
parts.detail: Water leaves the guide vanes with swirl and passes through the curved blades, giving up pressure and velocity as it turns the runner.

parts.name: Draft Tube
parts.short: Recovers velocity as the water leaves
parts.detail: The expanding tube slows the water and converts its remaining kinetic energy into a pressure difference that helps pull flow through the runner.

parts.name: Shaft
parts.short: Carries torque up to the generator
parts.detail: The vertical shaft connects the runner to the generator rotor and runs in guide bearings.

parts.name: Generator Stator
parts.detail: The stator surrounds the rotor. Changing magnetic flux induces voltage in its windings.

parts.name: Generator Rotor
parts.detail: The rotor carries the field poles and turns with the shaft at the grid's synchronous speed.

parts.name: Generator Top
parts.detail: The top housing carries the thrust bearing that supports the entire rotating mass.

parts.name: Exciter
parts.detail: The exciter feeds direct current to the rotor, controlling the generator's voltage and reactive power.

parts.name: Inlet Valve
parts.short: Isolates the turbine from the penstock
parts.detail: The valve closes to stop water for maintenance and is opened slowly to avoid a pressure surge.

parts.name: Governor
parts.detail: The governor moves the guide vanes to match load changes and keep frequency at 50 or 60 Hz.

parts.name: Cooling Coils
parts.detail: Water or air cooling carries away the losses in the stator and rotor.

parts.name: Work Lights
parts.detail: Lights around the casing let operators inspect the machine during maintenance.

parts.name: Nameplate
parts.detail: The plate records the design head, flow and rated output.

steps.title: The spiral spreads the flow
steps.body: Water enters the casing and wraps around the runner. The casing narrows as it goes, so the pressure stays even and every guide vane sees the same flow.

steps.title: Guide vanes set the power
steps.body: The guide vanes turn together to admit more or less water. That is the main control: more flow means more torque and more power.

steps.title: The runner takes the energy
steps.body: Water passes through curved blades and gives up pressure and velocity as it turns the runner. The shaft carries that torque to the generator.

steps.title: The draft tube recovers what is left
steps.body: Water leaves the runner fast. The expanding draft tube slows it, recovering pressure and helping pull flow through the machine instead of wasting the remaining energy.

quiz.prompt: Tap the part that directs water onto the runner blades.
Tap the part that recovers velocity as the water leaves.
Tap the rotating part of the generator.
Why does the spiral casing get smaller as it wraps around?
choices: To keep the flow even as water leaves through the vanes
quiz.explain: The shrinking section compensates for water leaving along the way, keeping pressure and flow uniform.

quiz.prompt: What do the guide vanes control?
choices: The water flow into the runner
quiz.explain: Opening or closing the guide vanes changes the flow and therefore the power.
